features.label: Grain reserves
features.help: Public granaries: each ruler keeps a granary in its regions with a stock target of a few turns of the region's food demand, more where its harvests swing; it buys real surplus toward the target, at market prices from the treasury, first in its own realm and then in foreign markets the merchants may reach, with transit and storage losses, and opens the granary in dearth or famine before hunger kills; needs an agent mode (default off; saved on resume)

features.label: Public grain shipments
features.help: Default-off public grain: foreign direct-neighbor orders arrive next Phase10, after its opening; requires --grain-reserves and agents. Disabling drains paid cargo.

features.label: Grain storage
features.help: Opt-in finite public storage with condition, timber/treasury costs and competing farmer work; requires hybrid granaries

features.label: Grain storage policy
features.help: Apply a storage policy to every region; saved policies otherwise persist

features.label: Scholarship
features.help: Seats of learning: rulers found academies at their capitals, temples found schools and cities libraries, kept by treasury, temple offerings or civic purse; scholars gather there (and scholar agents are drawn to them); a seat speeds the invention and adoption of techniques near it and keeps copies of the chronicles; a sack, a famine, persecution of its scholars' faith or unpaid upkeep brings it down, and its scholars flee to a rival's seat with the techniques they carry (default off; saved on resume)

features.label: Academy services
features.help: Default-off hybrid academy teaching: buys real supplies for next-turn native Scholar work; requires scholarship and techniques. Disabling pauses and retains supplies.

requires.reason: requires techniques (on by default for new worlds; off with --no-techniques)

features.label: Health care
features.help: Temporary occupational injuries and household care: lost work and care time constrain farming and work income; requires --agents hybrid (default off; saved state dormant in other modes)

features.label: Workshops
features.help: Staffed public workshops: up to four selected cities employ named adult urban farmers' already-diverted time; with --workshop-mode operate the controller's treasury pays construction and upkeep as a public cost (no wages) and the crew's work replaces the region's craft ceiling; requires --agents hybrid and cities (default off)

requires.reason: requires cities (on by default for new worlds; off with --no-cities)

features.label: Workshop mode
features.help: operate (default): treasury-funded crews replace the craft ceiling; observe: crews and native craft inputs only; cost_only: the ablation that builds and pays but keeps the legacy ceiling

features.label: Food allocation
features.help: Allocate each region's available food to its people and derived households under an explicit rule; individual hunger, needs and mortality read the person's own allocation; requires --agents hybrid (default off)

features.label: Food allocation regime
features.help: floor_means (default): an equal subsistence floor, the scarce remainder by household means; equal: equal per person (reproduces the regional signal); targeted_relief: equal market food, public granary release to the worst off

features.label: Timber stock
features.help: Renewable harvestable timber stock: realized timber extraction debits it, regrowth takes turns under forest cover and water, harvest cannot exceed it; requires an agent-backed economy (default off)

features.label: Grain convoys
features.help: Multi-leg public grain convoys: paid foreign purchases travel leg by leg, can be delayed, rerouted, turned back, captured or lost; requires --public-grain-shipments (default off)

features.label: Convoy route policy
features.help: adaptive (default), cheapest or safest route choice at dispatch

features.label: Commons rules
features.help: Commons rules on the timber stock: a region's controller may adopt a harvest quota with a rest period on a depleted, harvested stand, paying wardens from its treasury; partial payment leaves part of the stand open access; requires --timber-stock (default off)

features.label: Commons rule mode
features.help: enforced (default): the rule lowers the harvest cap; cost_only: the ablation that adopts and pays identically but applies no cap

features.label: Learning cohorts
features.help: Named learners at academies: finite cohorts of present adults attend actual delivered academy teaching, give up part of their ordinary income, and on completion gain skill in their trade; requires --agents hybrid and --academy-services (default off)

features.label: Learning cohort mode
features.help: learn (default): completion raises the learner's trade skill; no_learning: the cost-retaining control (same attendance, cost and supplies, no skill gain)

features.label: Workshop payroll
features.help: Workshop payroll (L6a): each operating workshop becomes a debt-free firm with cash and owned wares; an academy of the region's ruler (--academy-services) buys them with real treasury money, sales fund wages that replace the crew's ordinary income share, and unpaid wages cut hours, then crew, then close the firm; requires --workshops in operate mode (default off)

features.label: Workshop payroll mode
features.help: paid (default); unpaid_labor: the ablation that sells and replaces the income share but pays no wage; no_customer: wages are owed but nothing is sold

features.label: Relocation costs
features.help: Costly voluntary relocation (L7): an ordinary household move costs a fare per person (children included) that the adult movers must hold at the household gate and pay after the move is applied; requires --agents hybrid and no household-mobility liquid requirement (default off)

requires.reason: requires no household-mobility liquid requirement (--household-mobility-liquid-requirement unset or 0)

features.label: Relocation mode
features.help: paid (default); assisted: the destination's ruler funds a bounded share of the fare for households short of it; liquidity_only: the control that requires the fare but charges nothing

features.label: Local budgets
features.help: Local collective budgets: each ruler commits one finite projected budget to bargained envelopes for granary relief purchases, granary works and workshop bills; those services spend only within an accepted envelope; delivered or broken promises move the city's grievance; requires --agents hybrid and --grain-reserves (default off)

features.label: Local budget mode
features.help: bargained (default): constituencies' allocations arbitrated by influence, with political response; fixed_shares: the control, the same budget split by fixed declared shares, no bargaining and no response

features.label: Apprenticeship
features.help: Apprenticeship and skill continuity (RS1): qualified crew members mentor named apprentices at operating workshop sites; apprentices give up part of their ordinary income (a stipend with --workshop-payroll) and on completion earn a workshop qualification by stable id, kept for life; qualified people perform upkeep against site wear; requires --workshops in operate mode (--agents hybrid) (default off)

features.label: Apprenticeship mode
features.help: train (default): completion grants the qualification; no_qualification: the cost-retaining control (same wear, attendance and costs, no new qualifications)

features.label: Apprenticeship rules
features.help: RS1 rules version of a new apprenticeship state: 2 (default): attendance by region, portable progress, training on the job (PL2); 1: the recovery-skills phase's rules exactly (presence in the city box, seats before the crew, the consecutive-miss dropout). A saved state keeps its version; a conflicting value is refused on resume

features.label: Repair projects
features.help: Repair projects (RS2): paid projects rebuild workshop sites and granaries from their real condition and war damage, with named workers, timber and the controller's coins; they replace the L1 lump repair; requires --agents hybrid and --workshops or --grain-storage (default off)

features.label: Repair mode
features.help: repair (default): delivered work restores condition; cost_only: the cost-retaining control (reserves, pays and uses timber identically, condition unchanged)

features.label: Veteran reintegration
features.help: Veteran reintegration (RS3): soldiers released from real armies are recorded by stable id and get priority, among otherwise eligible candidates, for workshop crew, apprenticeship and repair openings; nothing is guaranteed or created; requires --agents hybrid and one of --workshops, --apprenticeship or --repair-projects (default off)

features.label: Veteran mode
features.help: priority (default): eligible veterans come first for openings; record_only: the control that captures and tracks veterans without priority

features.label: Remittances
features.help: Remittances (RS4): a diaspora ledger of applied migrations; settled migrants send a bounded share of their wealth along Marriage/Kin bonds to the region they left, with a courier fee and exactly-once receipts; requires --agents hybrid (default off)

features.label: Remittance mode
features.help: send (default); record_only: the control that keeps the ledger and sends nothing

features.label: Clearing protection
features.help: Funded clearing protection: a region's controller may protect up to two forested regions under population-driven clearing, paying wardens from its treasury for each turn the clearing is active; the paid share of the clearing is suspended at the ecology's clearing decision (native and Python); works in every agent mode (default off)

features.label: Clearing protection mode
features.help: enforced (default): the paid protection suspends clearing; cost_only: the control that adopts and pays identically but leaves the clearing unchanged

features.label: Operating wear
features.help: Workshop operating wear (PL2): each funded operating workshop site loses 0.02 condition a turn, offset only by the upkeep of qualified crew members (--apprenticeship); a worn site stops until repaired. --apprenticeship implies it; --workshops --operating-wear is the reference arm with the same maintenance assumption; requires --workshops in operate mode (--agents hybrid) (default off)

features.label: Timber supply
features.help: Timber supply (PL1): when RS2 repair projects lack timber, a named, paid crew of adults from the needing region (veterans first) walks to a forest of its civ or of nobody within two hops, cuts for a season and carries the timber home to the projects; their farm labour leaves the home economy, the harvest is debited from the L3 stock, wages come from the controller's treasury; requires --agents hybrid, --repair-projects and --timber-stock (default off)

features.label: Timber supply mode
features.help: supply (default); cost_only: the cost-retaining control (the same expeditions, crews, travel, wages and home labour removal, no cutting: no timber and no stock debit)

features.label: Timber orders
features.help: Cross-civilization timber procurement for measured repair gaps, real carrier purchases, finite escrow and delivery (default off).

features.label: Recovery crews
features.help: Recovery crews (PL3): granary repair work is done by a named crew of adult farmers resident in the granary's region, reserved for the turn and paid the granary's existing coins per work as wages by stable id (no new money); workshop repair crews draw on the site's whole region and admit eligible veterans of any non-enlisted occupation, their paid share withheld from ordinary income; requires --agents hybrid and --repair-projects (default off)

features.label: Recovery crew mode
features.help: paid (default): the granary coins go to the crew as wages; unpaid: the control with the same crews, income withheld and the same charge, the coins leaving the economy as before

features.label: Maintenance obligation
features.help: Maintenance obligation (PL3): before the L9 budget is bargained each ruler reserves its repair projects' planned per-turn charges, capped at a declared share of the budget; requires --local-budgets and --repair-projects (default off)

features.label: Maintenance obligation mode
features.help: reserve (default): repairs may spend the reservation beyond their bargained envelope; reserve_only: the crowding-out control that reserves the same amount but keeps repairs to their envelope and returns the reservation unspent

features.label: Household retail
features.help: Household food retail (L6b): in pilot regions most of each new harvest belongs to its farmers by stable id; owners' households eat their own food and sell the rest to neighbours at the clamped market price, buyers pay from their wealth, farmers' ordinary farm income is replaced by their sales; commons and granary releases stay free; requires --agents hybrid and --food-allocation (default off)

features.label: Household retail mode
features.help: retail (default); no_relief: the whole harvest titled, L2's rule on the commons, no means test; free_exchange: the same title and rounds at price 0 with farm income kept; record_only: the control that computes the pilot and the would-be title and changes nothing

features.label: Household retail boundary
features.help: market (default): each ruler's capital region, sticky; paid_work: regions where paid work has been done (an open workshop firm, a paid repair or granary crew, or the home of a paid woodcutting crew), sticky; all: every controlled region (stress)

features.label: Household retail rules
features.help: Retail rules version of a new retail state: 2 (default): each conquest, siege turn and occupation start destroys the share of pilot regions' owned food it destroys of their commons, once per event, recorded with its cause, actor and victim; 1: checkpoints 2-3 exactly (the conquest share once per turn, siege and occupation leave owned food alone). A saved state keeps its version; a conflicting value is refused

features.label: Watershed
features.help: Watershed account (B1): a conserved water account on the drainage graph rebuilt from the world's saved procedural elevation (precipitation, storage, evaporation, irrigation withdrawal, downstream transfer, outflow to the sea), with closure checked every turn, floods and droughts recorded with their conditions, and the water index the account would derive recorded beside the one the simulation uses; requires a procedural world (template worlds have no elevation); opens with a new world (default off)

requires.reason: requires a procedural world (template worlds have no elevation): in Batch Lab, a batch of more than 12 regions; on a live start, the run checks the requested world and refuses a template world (12 regions or fewer), reopening the lobby with the reason

features.label: Watershed mode
features.help: record_only (default): the account runs beside the existing water index and changes nothing outside its own record; flow: the account's derived index replaces the native water terms (climate terms, irrigation bonus, downstream deforestation cascade), upstream withdrawals reduce downstream water, and the account's floods act on capacity and soil while the old river flood is superseded; flow requires the native ecology

features.label: Workshop economics
features.help: Workshop economics (A3): each L6a workshop firm opens once with a capital payment from its region's ruler (no second firm at a closed firm's city), pays the ruler who owns the commons for the raw timber and ore it converts, before converting them, at the raw price the economy computed in an earlier tick, and sells wares to academies and, by stable id, to the region's households (adults pay); a site without a firm, or a firm that cannot pay for inputs, produces nothing; firms close when insolvent or idle; requires --workshop-payroll (default off)

features.label: Workshop economics mode
features.help: market (default); free_inputs: a diagnostic cost control only (free inputs are not a supported feature): every rule as market except that the input charge is recorded and not taken; academy_only: the demand control with no household customers

features.label: Workshop economics rules
features.help: Workshop economics rules version of a new state: 1 (default): A3-1 exactly (the tick's output enters the commons before title, so the people and merchants can use part of it free in the same tick); 2 (A3-2): a native column keeps each firm's output out of the commons, so it reaches anyone only by sale (households, academies) and the firm produces no more than its inventory room. A saved state keeps its version; a conflicting value is refused

features.label: Titled trade
features.help: Titled trade (A4): in household-retail pilot regions a resident merchant buys owners' food above their fair-share reserve, pro rata, at the local retail price, paying each owner by stable id; it carries the cargo with title and custody (one shipment by id, one edge a turn, its own model income withheld while it travels) to another pilot region within three hops where the price pays for the trip, and the delivered cargo becomes its retail claim sold to households; a conquest of the destination, a quarantine closure of the route or a lost route returns the shipment, the holder's death escheats the cargo to the commons where it stands; requires --agents hybrid and --household-retail in mode retail or no_relief with rules version 2 (default off)

features.label: Infrastructure condition
features.help: Infrastructure condition (B3): irrigation works and roads get a stable asset id, condition and service (s = min(1, condition / 0.5)); serving works wear each turn (irrigation 0.01, roads 0.005) and take war damage at conquest and sack; condition 0 fails a work until it is repaired; irrigation's arable-capacity bonus scales with service and its native flag and roads' two-hop trade range need service >= 0.5; works repair them with anonymous farm labour, timber and treasury coins planned after RS2's repairs (under --local-budgets only within their own envelope); requires --agents hybrid (default off)

requires.reason: requires one of: --infrastructure-condition-mode record_only or wear_only; --repair-projects

features.label: Infrastructure condition mode
features.help: repair (default; requires --repair-projects): works repair condition; record_only: condition is recorded and nothing else changes (service stays 1.0, no works); wear_only: wear and service act and nothing repairs (the control); cost_only (requires --repair-projects): works plan and pay identically and credit no condition

features.label: Harvest cover
features.help: Timber depletion opens canopy gaps without destroying standing stock; ecology owns regrowth and the watershed reads cover; requires --agents hybrid and --timber-stock (default off)

features.label: Harvest cover mode
features.help: loss (default): apply canopy gaps; record_only: observe proposed loss without changing cover

features.label: Epidemic care
features.help: Epidemic care (C2): each ruler may fund, from its local budget, carers for a region with a reported outbreak: adult farmers resident there who hold no other work, named by stable id, give their farm time (removed from farming, their ordinary income share withheld) for a wage paid from the treasury; the patients they can serve (5 per worker-turn) multiply case fatality at the next epidemic tick by 1 - 0.3 x coverage (one floor with practised medicine); requires --agents hybrid, --local-budgets and epidemiology with the contact ledger (default off)

requires.reason: requires epidemiology with the contact ledger (on by default for new worlds; off with --no-epidemiology or --no-contact-ledger)

features.label: Epidemic care mode
features.help: care (default): the carers' capacity lowers the next tick's case fatality; cost_only: the cost control with the same carers, farm time, withheld income and wages and no effect on fatality

features.label: Reform services
features.help: Poor relief as a real service (D1a): a granted poor relief no longer credits every agent's material need for grievance (the native reform table omits its rows); the treasury's relief payment (the upkeep, or the Commons Management share of the enforcement payment) goes into a relief fund (at most four turns of upkeep; the rest sunk as before) that buys the owners' unsold food, paid by stable id at the region's ask, where the realm's own pilot markets recorded people below a full ration, into the commons the next free rations draw on; the fund returns to the treasury when the relief ends; requires --agents hybrid, --household-retail (mode retail or no_relief) and agent movements (default off)

requires.reason: requires agent movements (on by default for new worlds; off with --no-agent-movements)

features.label: Reform services mode
features.help: service (default): the fund buys food for the next free pool; cost_only: the control that withholds the label and sinks the payment as without the switch, buying nothing

features.label: Guild leagues
features.help: Cross-border guild leagues (D1b): guilds of cities in different realms whose regions traded on 3 of the last 10 turns (the merchant deliveries the economy recorded) form a league (one member per realm, at most 4, ids never reused); each turn members pay 2 percent of their guild purse (at most 0.25) into the league fund while it holds less than 3 per member, and the fund pays a member city's purse its recorded levy share of the dues or the plunder of a recorded sack (at most 2 a claim); a member leaves when its guild or city ends or its city changes lord, and a league dissolves at war between members' realms, below two realms, or after 20 turns without trade, returning its fund to the members' purses; requires --agents hybrid, cities and guilds (default off)

requires.reason: requires cities (on by default for new worlds; off with --no-cities)
requires guilds (on by default for new worlds; off with --no-guilds)

features.label: Guild league mode
features.help: mutual (default): the fund pays recorded claims; dues_only: the cost control with the same leagues and dues and no claim paid

features.label: War requisition
features.help: D4 real army supply, seizure and treasury-funded restitution (default off); requires hybrid, campaigns and retail rules 2.

requires.reason: requires campaign armies (on by default; off with --no-campaigns)

features.label: War requisition mode
features.help: Saved option; choices ('transfer', 'cost_only')

features.label: War consequences
features.help: D3 combat wounds and dated family separation (default off); requires real army supply, health care and residence ledger.

features.label: War consequences mode
features.help: Saved option; choices ('active', 'record_only')

features.label: Adaptive livelihoods
features.help: A6 personal dated migration failures and work experience inform native decisions (default off); requires hybrid and residence ledger.

features.label: Adaptive livelihoods mode
features.help: Saved option; choices ('adapt', 'record_only', 'shuffled')

features.label: Adaptive livelihoods rules
features.help: 2 (unchanged default), 1: historical rules; explicit 3: independent war inputs and personal decision controls.

features.label: Adaptive livelihoods decision channels
features.help: Rules3 personal controls: all (default), no_migration_experience, no_information (migration knowledge), no_work, no_trade. War inputs stay independent.

features.label: Public health
features.help: Supplied epidemic care, maintained-water sanitation, physical density and dated public-health advice (default off).

features.label: Public health mode
features.help: Saved option; choices ('active', 'cost_only')

features.label: Public health policy
features.help: Saved option; choices ('evidence', 'shuffled')

features.label: Public health crowding
features.help: legacy_displacement (unchanged default): historical classified X1 multiplier; explicit density_only: existing physical density only, no motive multiplier.

features.label: Movement branches
features.help: Dated movement branches abroad funded by named local members (default off).

requires.reason: requires agent movements (on by default for new worlds; off with --no-agent-movements)

features.label: Movement branches mode
features.help: funded (default): paid local permission; cost_only: identical dues without permission; record_only: no payment or native effect.

features.label: Residence ledger
features.help: Residence ledger (X1, the displacement contract): a record-only ledger of where each person lives, where they belong and why they left: home (the residence when first observed, changed only by a voluntary or unclassified move of a person who is not displaced, or after 20 turns settled elsewhere; never by enlistment), residence, army attachment and displacement spells opened by a flight- or hunger-driven move from home, with the opening driver and the home-region event (war, famine, persecution) dated in the 5 turns before, kept open by any onward move and closed on return, resettlement, death, a rebuilt pool or an unobserved gap; one frame per turn dated by its source turn, readable by a consumer only the next turn; changes nothing; requires --agents hybrid (default off)

features.label: Attribution records
features.help: Attribution records (D2): observation-only records of who did what to whom, at the event: granary seizures with their actor and victim; enlisted soldiers' deaths per war and cause - combat, attrition, war drain (found dead after the tick in a region where a siege, garrison fight, occupation, crushed revolt, nomad raid or a roster-less army's losses staged deaths that turn, at most the staged count; possibly_enemy when no single actor is named) and natural (the other deaths army casualties include: native mortality with its x2 for soldiers at war, plague and other non-war catastrophes); each reuse of a civilization index by a restored polity; and the burdens one polity lays on another per turn (dues, levies, sacks, plunder, requisitions, seizures, war losses, treaty payments, quarantine closures), each labelled by its authority and as a transfer, minted, destroyed or a restriction; nothing reads them; requires --agents hybrid (default off)

features.label: Wealth accounting
features.help: Wealth accounting (A1): an observation-only ledger of agent wealth; each turn and region it reads the balance at the Phase 2 opening (checked bit for bit against the last closing) and after every payer, records the typed flows from the packages' receipts (wages, stipends, purchases, procurement, remittances, fares, domestic credit), the paid-work income each package withheld and the treasury side, and labels the rest as unitemized native model flows; changes nothing; requires --agents hybrid (default off)

features.label: Wealth accounting mode
features.help: observe (default): itemized source/sink ledger; strict: refuse an unexplained balance closure.

features.label: Quarantine mode
features.help: Quarantine rules (connected-world C1): legacy (default, the same as omitting it, needs nothing): the abstract import multiplier and a flat charge; none: no quarantine; cost_only: the same decisions and enforcement cost as closure, nothing restricted; closure: trade routes and agent merchant edges between a closing polity and each polity with a reported outbreak it is in contact with are closed while the outbreak is reported, at a declared enforcement cost, with no import multiplier (relief grain, armies and hostages stay open; migrants too unless --quarantine-channels trade,migration); none, cost_only and closure require epidemiology and the contact ledger; saved on the world (docs/integration/quarantine-rules.md)

any.reason: requires epidemiology with the contact ledger (on by default for new worlds; off with --no-epidemiology or --no-contact-ledger)

requires.reason: requires one of: epidemiology with the contact ledger (on by default for new worlds; off with --no-epidemiology or --no-contact-ledger); --quarantine-mode legacy

features.label: Quarantine channels
features.help: Journeys --quarantine-mode closure restricts (connected-world C1b): trade (default, the same as omitting it): trade routes and agent merchant edges; trade,migration: also refuses native migrations between the two polities of each closed pair, either way, while the closure lasts (refugees included, counted apart; moves already made stay); trade,migration requires --quarantine-mode closure and an agent mode in which the native pool owns the population (hybrid or demographics-only; not shadow, whose Python population still migrates); saved on the world (docs/integration/quarantine-rules.md)

requires.reason: requires one of: --quarantine-channels trade; --agents hybrid or demographics-only
